newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's 96-97 coffee output may fall 20 percent.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's 96-97 coffee output may fall 20 percent.

text.p: Mexico's 1996-1997 coffee crop is expected to fall about 20 percent compared with the previous harvest, a spokesman for the National Coordinating Council of Coffee Organizations told Reuters Monday.

The association of small Mexican coffee farmers had predicted a 10 percent fall from last year's coffee output because of the harvest cycle, but freezes in December further lowered the group's estimates, council spokesman Luis Hernandez said..
"To begin with last year's crop was exceptional and harvests have good and bad cycles," he said.

A lack of rains in principal coffee producing state Chiapas hurt crops there, and December's freezing temperatures in higher altitudes of Veracruz and Puebla states also cut output, he said. Hernandez said the council's members have not yet assessed damage to crops from freezing temperatures in recent weeks.
Farmers received less financing and credit for planting from government and private banks, he said, and lower coffee prices additionally discouraged plentiful crops.
"Also it is related to lower than hoped for prices and the danger that prices would continue falling," Hernandez said.
